utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I deal with a few matters. I do understand that the Prosecution wanted to raise that P3761 was not fully uploaded into e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's correct. And that we'd ask that the court officer be instructed to replace the current version of Exhibit P3761 with the revised version uploaded under 65 ter 03098A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now I have no recollection, but I would have to look at it, whether we considered that we were invited or at least that we were expected to admit more than what was uploaded at the time. Could you tell us what the document is and what is now added, what was missing?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd have to check and I can further report back at the outset of the next break. I do know that it stems from a decision on the Prosecution motion for admission of documents from the bar table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that. I even could tell that you it's -- apparently it's the Serbian Republic Ministry --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of Interior Sarajevo, Security Services Centre, Banja Luka, with a number, information in connection with dispatch number 11. So we have a description. But, of course, what I'm wondering is what --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- did we look at when we admitted it and what is now extra.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What is, I'm being informed is, extra is that the -- there's a full list of prisoners that we would like to attach that relates to the document which was not uploaded previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then may I take it that Defence will have a look at it as well, whether the list of prisoners is something that needs further attention yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Sarenac. Perhaps you are a bit surprised to see three Judges rather than two.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yesterday I was, for urgent reasons, unable to sit. That's the reason why you saw two Judges yesterday and why you see three again today. I read that you were reminded by Judge Moloto yesterday that you should not speak with anyone. I now remind you to something different; that is, that you gave a solemn declaration yesterday that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. I'd remind you that you're still bound by that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P4583 for the witness, page 278 of the B/C/S original and page 324 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Sarenac, I didn't mean to ignore you, but just for expediency I calling out the number. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Coming up before you will be -- I see that we're not in the English correct spot yet. Coming up -- well, what's before you now is part of President Karadzic's statements at the 50th National Assembly of Republika Srpska held on the 15th and 16th of April, 1995, in Sanski Most. Yesterday we left off discussing the operations in Kupres in early April 1992, and I'd like to read a portion of his statements to you now. Toward the bottom of the page in front of you --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, this ask in the middle of the translation, middle of the page in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- President Karadzic states: "Gentlemen, we got the officers we asked for. I asked for Mladic. General Ninkovic, then a Colonel, and General Perisic had visited me before that, and I had noticed Mladic's blunt statements in the newspapers. He was already in Knin then."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please have the next page of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: "I took an interest in him and together with Krajisnik, I went to General Kukanjac's office and listened to him issuing orders and commanding around Kupres and Knin. We spent countless nights in the office of General Kukanjac at the time [sic]." Were you aware that President Karadzic had listened to General Mladic's orders around Kupres from General Kukanjac's office.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time that I hear of it. I'd never heard it before, nor did I know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you. We're done with this document. Sir, I'm going to move on an and discuss some other things with you. I want to discuss with you the 1st Guards Motorised Brigade. In paragraph 9 of your statement, you state the 1st Guards Brigade: "Received all orders from the VRS Main Staff (from the commander and the Chief of Staff)." Is it correct that all orders to the 1st guards Motorised Brigade came from General Mladic and General Milovanovic?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it did happen, and I'm trying to recall it, that we were attached to some unit, for instance, to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps or some other unit, then we would -- it would be possible for us to receive orders directly from them; in other words, from the units that -- whose complement we were part of, temporarily at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do I understand correctly that absent you being specifically resubordinated to another corps, that your orders came from either General Mladic or General Milovanovic?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that would be the regular way. However, if we were resubordinated to somebody else, for instance, to a -- the commander or the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, in that case, we could receive orders from the commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps or whoever else, whichever other unit we were resubordinated to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P4995 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Sarenac, this is a 12 January 1993 VRS Main Staff order on the establishment of the 1st Guards Motorised Brigade from General Mladic and signed for him by General Milovanovic. In the beginning of the order, there's reference to another order dated 15 December 1992 from the commander of the Army of Republika Srpska which was done at the request of the Supreme Commander. Is it correct that General Mladic ordered the establishment of the 1st Guards Brigade in December 1992 after a request from President Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there at the time, and I didn't have occasion to see this document, so I really can't tell you anything about that. This is the first time that I see this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe you can help us with the next paragraph then. The order discusses three purposes of the Guards Brigade. The third purpose states: "To allow the Supreme Command to directly intervene in case of a threat to vital axes, sectors or features." Is it correct that the 1st Guards Motorised Brigade was a manoeuvre unit, meaning that it was intended for deployment and use in any part of the territory of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you aware that the formation of the 1st Guards Brigade was completed by 19 January 1993?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the -- somebody's wishful thinking. However, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go through some things then. Before doing so I just want to go over the Command Staff structure. In 1993 and 1994, the commander of the 1st Guards Brigade was Colonel Milenko Lazic; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first commander was Colonel Rajak, the second was Colonel Lasic, the third Lieutenant-Colonel Lalovic, and I don't think I need to name all the others. The fourth was Samardzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You mentioned Mirko Trivic in your statement. Mirko Trivic was the deputy commander of the brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the chief and also the deputy brigade commander up until about the summer of 1994, when he was reassigned as commander of the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear what brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and replaced by Lieutenant-Colonel Lalovic, Dragan.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the brigade --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, may I interrupt you for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sure, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The witness mentioned four commanders of the brigade. The fourth name is not recorded because he said: "... I don't think I need to name all the others." But then he mentioned the fourth name. It should be put on the record what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Sarenac, did you hear Judge Fluegge's question? And if you could repeat the last commander of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear it. It was Zdravko Samardzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And the interpreters didn't hear the name of the brigade that the witness referred to at line 23 or 24 of page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You were speaking about Mirko Trivic, sir, and you said he was reassigned as commander of the, and then it cuts off. Could you please repeat what you -- the last part of your sentence was.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that about Mirko Trivic? Lieutenant-Colonel Mirko Trivic when I arrived at the brigade was the Chief of Staff and also the deputy commander in the brigade. He remained at that post until the summer of 1994. In the summer of 1994 he was reassigned as commander of one of the brigades of the Herzegovina Corps and was replaced by major, who had already been a member of the brigade, Djurdjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, you were the assistant commander for morale and religious affairs of the brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And to clarify it, the question by Judge Moloto was not properly answered. That was all about the 1st Guards Motorised Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm not sure -- what do you mean all this was about? What I mentioned about Trivic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No. You told us the four commanders of the brigade, but the name of the brigade wasn't mentioned. Is that the 1st Guards Motorised Brigade what you are talking about, about the four commanders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am talking about the 1st Guards Motorised Brigade. The brigade that I was a member of as assistant commander for morale, information, and legal issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think this is now clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And I appreciate the assistance. I'm flipping back and forth on the screen here and I don't have the separate LiveNote, so I really do appreciate the assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We know that there is a problem with LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, Zeljko Stupar was the assistant commander for intelligence and security in the brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Unfortunately, he is deceased.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 1061 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, coming up will be a 24 January 1993 VRS Main Staff order from General Mladic concerning the initial deployment of the 1st Guards Brigade. When it comes up --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And if we could maybe have it even enlarged for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- could you please review item 1 of the order and confirm that your brigade was composed of the battalions described in the document?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a per establishment of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The order indicates that there was a mechanised battalion and two motorised battalions in your brigade. Is it correct that the Guards Brigade possessed tanks and armoured vehicles?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There's also a reference to a mixed artillery battalion. Is it correct that your brigade possessed 120-millimetre mortars and pieces of artillery?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Some artillery pieces but all right, you could say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 1061 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number for 65 ter 1061 would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number P6927, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6927 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Sarenac, I now want to discuss with you operations of the 1st Guards Brigade in the spring of 1993 in Eastern Bosnia. You discuss these operations in paragraphs 11 to 16 and in paragraph 18 of your statement. Before we discuss them, my question is: Is it correct that the brigade was deployed to the areas of Cerska, Bratunac, Skelani, and Srebrenica between March and the end of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade was sent from where it was accommodated. It was sent to various missions, according to orders from the Main Staff. So I don't understand your question when you say was it deployed there. It wasn't just deployed. We were directly involved. We would be sent to carry out the mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. The missions you carried out were in the areas Cerska, Bratunac, Skelani, and Srebrenica; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At the end of paragraph 11 of your statement, you state that: "After successful combat activities, we were sent to liberate Serb villages between Bratunac and Srebrenica." Is it correct that this was after your -- as you're describing it, mission, in Cerska and after Cerska was liberated?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During the VRS operations to take over the areas of Cerska and Konjevic Polje, Muslim civilians were escaping from these areas toward Tuzla or Srebrenica. You were aware of this; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we didn't fight the civilians. We fought the armed units of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear what brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But if someone happened to be in the way, that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the question was whether you were aware of civilians escaping. The question was not whether you attacked civilians. The question is whether you are aware of civilians escaping.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I wasn't aware of it. I was not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you that, in fact, the VRS units attacked and shelled Muslim civilians who were passing through VRS lines. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember any such cases. After all, the 1st Guards Motorised Brigade was not the only unit that was there to carry out a combat mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 09563 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, when you emphasise that the 1st Guards Motorised Brigade was not the only unit there, do you say, well, it may have been others, or do you say I'm not aware that it happened at all, or do you say it may have happened but then it must have been some other unit? It's not clear to me what you meant by emphasising this fact.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let's be clear on this. Why would there be civilians in an area where there were combat operations? That's one thing. And secondly, I did not know of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So the first question is why they should be there. If you don't know whether they were, is it -- not a question you possibly could give us an answer to. Therefore, also not useful to raise. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a combat report from Vinko Pandurevic dated 2 March 1993, and I want to direct your attention to the first part of it. In this document, the command of the Zvornik brigade informs the Drina Corps command that at around 8.30 hours, columns of civilians and soldiers with pack animals were noticed from Udrc and Rasevo towards Konjevic Polje, and it indicates the columns were hit with every available means. Sir, your brigade was operating in this area. How is it that you are not aware that the VRS shelled and attacked the columns that included Muslim civilians during these operations?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Misquote. Where it says the Guards Brigade operated in this direction along this axis. Cerska is a far broader area than the one referred to in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the brigade operated in -- I went through multiple areas at this time, so this is a fair question, including --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you could make it very specific and then rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm not sure in what way I can make it more specific aside to ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- could you explain to me how you're not aware of the Zvornik Brigade using all available means against Muslim civilians -- well, columns that included Muslim civilians? You were active as part of operations in this area at the time; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the commander of the Zvornik Brigade, and he is sending a report about the activities of his brigade. There's no reference to the Guards Brigade here, so I disassociate myself from any report. I am not familiar with that report of his, and I did not know that he did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So do you allow for the possibility that the Zvornik Brigade undertook these activities during the operations in Eastern Bosnia in March 1993?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I do not know. His superior command knows. I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, sir, we'll come to some other documents. But, in fact, you were acting in co-ordination with the Drina Corps at this time; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but everybody had his own area of responsibility and area of operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, The Prosecution would tender the document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 9563 receives number P6928, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6928 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 12 of your statement, you discuss the Kevaric [phoen] hill by Srebrenica. Is it correct that your brigade broke through to the Kevaric hill on 16 April 1993 and put the flag of Republika Srpska on the TV relay there?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that is correct because -- well, you're asking for a precise date or something else. Well, that's the way it was. And nothing further.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, you don't always have to explain. I'm going to try to ask you very specific questions so we can move through things. In May 1993 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You put a date and an event together.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then what the witness tells us, that that is approximately how it went, but apparently he may be -- he asked whether the specific date you mentioned was -- was what you were seeking to have confirmed and that is, of course, because of your question. And therefore, in all fairness to the witness I think he was, under those circumstances, he should have asked in view of his own knowledge, not knowing practical -- exactly the date but knowing that these kind of events went on during those days. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. And, Your Honour, I was actually trying to be fair to the witness. I'm sorry if I didn't clarify that. I knew that he was trying to explain. I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, in May 1993 your brigade took part in the liberation of Zepa and Gorazde; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In May 1993? Well, yes. Well, it's not the liberation of Zepa and Gorazde. It is combat operations around Zepa and around Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P4324 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 1 May 1993 VRS Main Staff combat order for the liberation of Zepa and Gorazde from General Milovanovic. We see on this front page that it was addressed to several commands, including the Drina, Herzegovina, and Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. Your brigade and the Visegrad Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please go actually directly to page 6 of the B/C/S original and page 8 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At the top of the page before you --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, this is at the bottom of the page in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- there's the section on the tasks of the units. According to the first task, the Drina Corps, reinforced by the 1st Guards Brigade and other formations --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please have the next page of the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- are tasked to: "... swiftly come out to the right bank of the river Drina, liberate Zepa and Gorazde, and put Gorazde and the entire Podrinje region under their control." These were your orders at the time; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we received orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You received these orders; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please go to page 10 of the English translation. And for the witness, if we could go to the bottom of the page before him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, at the bottom of the page before you, which is in the bottom half of the translation, the order indicates that the 1st Gmtbr along with one battalion of the 1st Podrinje brigade and another company shall attack in the direction of Zepa. Your brigade carried out this attack; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the brigade acted in accordance with the given task at Kasik [phoen]. Zepa itself was not attacked but this was the route that was taken. But the ultimate objective was not reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please go to page 7 of the original and page 11 of the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the upper third of the page before you, the order goes on to instruct: "Upon the liberation of the wider region of Zepa, the civilian population shall be provided with the organised exit to the premises of the so-called Central Bosnia." This was also part of your brigade's orders; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it would be fair to read the entire sentence to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the witness answered the question already. But if you think that further context is needed, re-examination is, of course, the most appropriate moment to add whatever context you consider relevant, Mr. Stojanovic. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P5173 for the witness. I didn't know if Your Honours had any other questions on the last document. I'm sorry I didn't ask before moving on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. One second, please. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P5173.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Sarenac, this is a 22 May 1993 VRS Main Staff combat order for the liberation of the general area of Gorazde from General Mladic. This document was sent to the commands of the Drina and Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and the command of the 1st Guards Brigade. We can see that on the front page here. And if we could in the translation go down to item 2. Under item 2, General Mladic orders: "The task of the Army of RS is to carry out offensive operations and" -- in the original, it says "ocisti," "central Podrinje. Disperse and destroy Muslim armed forces in the general area of Gorazde and enable the Muslim civilians to move away (relocate) to other areas (central part of the former BiH) or to accept ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And could we have the next page of the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: "... the authority of Republika Srpska and thus create conditions for the return of the Serbian population to the left and right banks of the Drina River." Sir, these were your tasks during the liberation of Gorazde; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are tasks that were given to all the units that took part in the liberation. Well, I cannot say Gorazde. It's not that we were liberating Gorazde. In these offensive activities, we did not enter Gorazde. We were stopped. Otherwise, that had been the order of the superior command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, unfortunately the question doesn't relate to what happened on the ground. The question is were these your orders. I think you can either say, yes, these were our orders, or no, these were not our orders.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we received an order, no doubt. It can be seen here in the content --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you received this order. Not just an order. This one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, right now, while I'm reading it, if it's identical then this is the order we received. That order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If it's identical to what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if it's identical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Identical to what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If it's the identical order. I mean, I don't know whether it's a forgery or some other form of document. But if this order has to do with offensive combat operations in the specific case of Gorazde, then we received that order. I don't have that order here with me in my pocket. I am reading this now just as you are reading it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second, just a second. You are not being asked to tell us whether this is identical to the order that you received. You are being asked whether you can remember from your own memory that this order is exactly the same order as the one you received during combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And perhaps in order to further clarify, the order being liberating Gorazde. Because the document may say a few other things as well, but we are focusing on the liberation of Gorazde. Did you receive an order -- do you remember to have received an order to liberate Gorazde?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember that we were carrying out a combat mission towards Gorazde and that order was received by the Guards Brigade; that is to say, we received an order because without an order we would not be carrying out such combat operations vis-a-vis Gorazde, say from Rudo to Gorazde. I mean, I don't know now -- I mean, from Rogatica towards Gorazde, things like that. So we did receive an order and it is on the basis of that order that we acted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then you were stopped. You were unable to liberate Gorazde, if I understand you well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] International forces entered Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P3071, 3-0-7-1.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Sarenac, this is a 30 May 1993 VRS Main Staff report on the conclusions from the assessment of the situation. The report mainly addresses the situation in the Podrinje throughout the spring of 1993. So you are aware, the document was recovered along with some of General Mladic's notebooks in the year 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 3 of the original and page 4 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, on this page we see the section on strategic and operative situation and problems. This is on the lower half of the page in front of you. In the second paragraph of this section, the report states: "Representatives of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska have been in the zone of operations of the Drina Corps since January this year, who comprise the IKM, are focused on planning further operations, and they are commanding certain operations in order to carry out the task set, which is the liberation of the entire area of Podrinje." Is it correct that General Mladic was one of the VRS Main Staff representatives commanding from positions in the Podrinje; specifically, Drina Corps forward command posts?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, and I am not aware of General Mladic being at the forward command post. I am unaware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What Main Staff representatives are you aware of?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about them being there either. I was on a combat mission with my own unit, and after all I didn't have the right to ask around as to who was where.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. The next paragraph discusses how this task is being carried out through tactically separate battles. The end of the paragraph states: "This achieves the strategic objective formulated in the stand." And then there's a subquote: "So that the river Drina is not the border towards Serbia." Sir, the combat operations you were a part of was furthering this strategic objective; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My task is to carry out that task. In this specific case, a combat mission without being involved in any kind of politics.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you about politics. That was the strategic objective of the battles that you were a part of. Were you aware of that or not?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that I was on a combat mission. Now, if you are asking me about the strategic objective further on, to tell you the truth, I don't know. I wouldn't know how to answer that question. I know what I did, where I was, and who I was with. As for political events, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the question has been answered. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know if this a good time for a break or I could keep on going. It's -- I'm going to be on this document for a little bit longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it's perhaps wiser that we interrupt here and that you will --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- continue after the break. Could first the witness be escorted out of the courtroom. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we take that break, the Chamber is puzzled by P3761, what you wanted to attach. It is a short report with a list of -- a two-page list of names attached of prisoners from Kljuc. The Annex A to the Prosecution motion to admit evidence from the bar table, municipalities component, gives as the ERN range in English 0301-8622 to 0301-8624. That means three pages. Yes, three pages: 22, 23, 24. What is at this moment in e-court in both languages is a three-page document, the first page being a document dated the 20th of -- the 29th of August, 1992; the second and the -- or let me just have a look. Yes, the second and the third page list of 67 names. So the Chamber is puzzled by what is there newly now to be uploaded which is not yet in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could, if we could -- I'm not quite fully familiar with it, I'm just reading off of some other stuff here. If we could address it at the outset of the next break --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- that would be greatly appreciated just so we could correctly inform you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's in itself okay. I reminded the Defence several times that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- they should not just read out things they had not verified themselves --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and we are not adopting such an approach because we're asking ourselves what you are presenting to us, what does it mean, what is it exactly what you want us to do; that is, to admit two additional pages of -- or include in what we admit the two pages. The same what I said several times to the Defence is even if a text is prepared for you, it's your responsibility to verify it because you start reading it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's we'll understood and I agree with you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I can't say that I myself always fully perform that but at least I try to do my utmost best to try to understand what we are talking about. If that is clear to you, then you have 20 minutes of rest, Mr. Weber, to think about it. Although you have done that already. We resume at -- Yes, Mr. Traldi, you are there, I take it...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd come down to address the document, Your Honour, and it's my error this morning, of course. But can I briefly provide our explanation to the Chamber if that suits you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, since I have it in front of me at this moment and since we dealt with it, if you could do it in one or two minutes, then we would appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, our annex to the bar table motion that you were referring to a moment ago explained the relevance of this document, I think it's at page 87, by noting that the document reflects that at least 1.161 non-Serbs had been transferred from Kljuc to Manjaca camp. That's reflected by the full list now uploaded as 03098A and by the attachment at the end of the full list. It's not uploaded -- it's not reflected by the introductory page and the partial two pages of the list which were uploaded as 65 ter 03098 and subsequently were admitted as Exhibit P03761. So both -- so the ERN range that we set out in the motion correctly reflected what had been uploaded, but both the ERN range and the upload referred only to part of the document and to part of the document that did not fully reflect what we informed the Chamber we were seeking to tender and did not fully reflect the basis for which we were seeking to tender the document. I had spoken briefly to Mr. Lukic about this this morning and had been informed that the Defence didn't object, but I'm not sure. I haven't spoken to him in the last hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, in light of the motion we didn't -- we said to the Prosecution that we do not object to admission of this whole document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which means the whole document, not only the first two pages of the list but the full list, so as to establish or at least to seek to establish the full number of Kljuc prisoners that were detained at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Of course what it establishes is a matter for the Chamber to evaluate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No, that's -- that's why I said "seeking to establish." I have chosen my words in view of what you just said. One second, please. Yes, my mistake. We were under the impression that it was about a -- the English version only, but that's not the case. And that also could not deduced from the e-mail which was sent in relation to this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I should say that's my fault as well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I say that the e-mail is correct where the misunderstanding comes from. Perhaps we haven't read it sufficiently. Madam Registrar, you are hereby instructed to replace what is now known in e-court as P3761, in both languages only three pages, now to be replaced by 65 ter 03098a, which should be the same document with additional pages containing the list of prisoners from Kljuc. We resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I did have one other housekeeping matter that we maybe can address quickly. It relates P6926 which was admitted yesterday. After court yesterday, the translation booth notified the Prosecution of a translation error in the end of the first sentence of the quote that was read in, that it should at the end of the sentence read "and Serbian army." We greatly appreciate the translation booth notifying of us of this and we wanted to inform the Chamber that that's been brought to our attention and we've also requested a revised translation, and then we'll further inform the Chamber when that's available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I take it that there's no problem with that as far as the Defence is concerned. There was another matter, I think with P6126, that parties wanted to make further submissions, if I remember well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I misspoke, 6925. I think there was a wish to make further submission on admission, I think it was. I think it was the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's the newspaper article from Vreme.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Newspaper article. First of all, I think the parties would still consider where Vreme was published. That it was Serbian seemed not to be in dispute but where it was published. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wasn't in court yesterday when this was discussed and I'm not sure what the status of the discussions are between Mr. Jeremy and the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll wait for a further report on that and we'll not forget about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please go to page 1 in the B/C/S original and page 2 of the English declaration in the document before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, we left off discussing this VRS Main Staff report from the 30th of May 1993, and I would like to focus on a couple other sections of it with you. Earlier in this report, there's a discussion of the situation in the Podrinje. I'd like to direct your attention to the bottom of the page before you, which is the first full paragraph in the translation. The paragraph starts: "The loss of most of the Podrinje and intensive combat operations in the general sector," and then there's four villages that are referenced, "and other places in the Drina valley has provoked fear or even panic among the Muslim soldiers and population ..." Is it correct that this was the result of the VRS operations you were a part of?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is an assessment, someone's assessment. And I believe that it is partially correct because everyone is afraid of war. And the people from that area, they surely were anxious and they were surely afraid, especially among the civilians there was a lot of fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please go forward to page 4 of the B/C/S and page 5 of the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to be directing your attention towards the bottom of the page. On this page we see three main problems that are listed. This is after a discussion of how the VRS had to halt operations on 17 April due to pressure from public opinion. I just want to draw your attention to the third problem that states: "Preventing the Muslim population from returning to previously abandoned villages and towns." After this list of problems, there is a discussion of possibilities for further operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have the next page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, in the middle of the page --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, this is also in the middle of the page in the English, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- the report states: "Our tactical moves and propaganda should develop in them the feeling that they live in ghetto-type enclaves and that their destiny depends on the Serbian people and the Army of the RS. This influence should result in the population in these areas and sectors gradually moving out, with those who moved out before being reluctant to return." The next paragraph then states: "This means that attack operations in Podrinje are possible and much needed in order to take important land features, inflict losses on the Muslim forces outside the demilitarised zones, and create general insecurity among soldiers and the population as a result of living in complete encirclement and isolation in the so-called safe areas." Sir, after May 1993, the objective of the VRS was still to have the Muslim population move out by making their lives unbearable in ghetto-type enclaves, including Srebrenica, Zepa, and Gorazde; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not the case. And for the reason that the areas were declared demilitarised areas, and the disarming of the combat troops was supposed to be finalized in all areas in Podrinje, in which case there would be no provocation of the Serbian side. Again, they wouldn't provoke the Serbian side into carrying out attacks because throughout this period, they kept attacking the Serbian army, the Serbian population, from those areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So their fighters --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you that your evidence is contradicted by the VRS Main Staff documents that we've been looking at; the two orders and also this report. And I also add --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm putting my case, Your Honours. If I could finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And I also note that -- I put it to you that you were actually a part of these propaganda activities as an assistant commander in morale guidance and religious affairs. So I put it to you that your answers are not credible -- that your answer is not credible, the one you just gave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you answer the question, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. Firstly, the Prosecutor claims that this is a Main Staff document. Now from the document we have before us, we can see either the signature or the stamp or the author of this document on the last page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is comment on discussing the content of the document, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, okay. I won't comment. I just have an objection. We don't have a chain of custody of this document, the source of this document, how it was obtained. All of this should be cleared up before the witness should give his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Mr. Stojanovic, this is -- there's something -- well, yes. Mr. Stojanovic, this is a document in evidence. You can't just now start challenging the authenticity. I don't know whether it was done at the time, I don't know whether we ruled specifically on that, that's one. So that's inappropriate to do. Second, the document -- the heading reads: "Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska." For that reason alone, Mr. Weber is entitled to put the document as he did to the witness. So both objections, the first one is denied. The second is an inappropriate challenge to the authenticity of this document which is in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And therefore to the extent that is a objection to the question, and I wonder whether it is, but if you understand it like that, it's denied. Mr. Weber put it to you that what you're telling is contradicted by this document and other documents he has shown to you. And he has put to you what the position of the Prosecution is, that these were the real objectives as described in those documents and that you were part - in your function - part of that, and perhaps you take over here, you were part of that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: As the assistant commander for morale, religious, and legal affairs in your brigade, that you were a part of promulgating this feeling within the Muslim population in the enclaves.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in a position to do that either in terms of the equipment that I had or the technical assets that I had at my disposal to be able to carry out something like that. So absolutely not. How could I do this on the Muslim side? What -- what could I use? A radio? I didn't have a radio set. TV? None. Any kind of loud-speaker system, no. We didn't have any of that. We didn't have any of that at our disposal. So we did not have the technical means to carry that out. Had we wanted to do so, we would still not have been able because we had nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we do have some other evidence about other events later on. I was going to then move on to another topic. I don't know if you have any other questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Proceed as you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, in paragraphs 19 to 22 of your statement, you discuss joint operations with the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps in July and August 1993. Is it correct that the operation you were discussing is Operation Lukavac 1993 -- or, I'm sorry, Operation Lukavac 93.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What operation am I talking about? Well, I'm just answering questions. We can broach the topic of Lukavac 93.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm just asking you to clarify that the operation that you're talking about in your statement when you're referring to events that you were a part of in July and August 1993 that you're talking about Lukavac 93?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 31616 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 11 July 1993 SRK command order from General Galic to continue combat operations in accordance with the Lukavac 93 plan. We see that this order was sent to multiple brigades, including the Guards Brigade, from the IKM. Is it correct that this IKM was on Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so, but where exactly this post was, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, in paragraph 19 of your statement you state that the brigade was tasked to act jointly with the SRK from the region of Jahorina mountain, and then you say: "(Bijele Vode)." This was the location of the IKM; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the forward or the beginning line where we were actually introduced to combat. Now, where the forward command post of the Sarajevsko Romanija Brigade was, I really don't know. Most probably in Lukavica, but I don't know. I don't know if it was on Mount Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's on in that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under item 4.1 of this order General Galic orders the 1st Sarajevo Mechanised Brigade, which is noted as Smbr, to hold the town of Sarajevo, and the translations says "under siege" but I see in the original it says "blokadi," and provide on the axis of Lucevic [phoen] in a co-ordinated action with the 2nd Sarajevo Brigade, which is noted as the 2nd Slpbr.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we have the next page in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: General Galic then states: "After the 1st gmtbr," your brigade, "comes out and seized the Pijevac and Bojista feature. They shall capture the general area of Lucevik in a co-ordinated action with the 1st Gmtbr, thus liberating the Trnovo-Sarajevo road." Sir, these were your orders at this time; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were orders that we received, the 1st Guards Motorised Brigade, and pursuant to this order there would follow orders from our commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The town of Sarajevo was being kept under blockade by the SRK while you carried out these operations in Trnovo; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know anything about that. I was not a member of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. In this particular case, we were attached to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, but only for the combat mission on --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, could you finish the last part of your statement, "but only for the combat mission on..." Did you mention a location?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that we received orders -- or this order was received, this order from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps was received, it wasn't our order. Now, based on this order we then issued our own order to carry out a combat mission towards Trnovo. So from Jahorina on -- onto Trnopolje. I don't know if you understand me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I do. Thank you for that clarification. In paragraph 20 of your statement, you refer to the specific date 11 July 1993 and state that my unit, together with part of the SRK units, entered Trnovo headed by the VRS Main Staff commander. The other SRK units that you were referring to were the 1st Sarajevo Mechanised Brigade and the 2nd Sarajevo Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know -- I know how we went to Trnovo and with whom. But as for the arrival of various brigade, they arrived after us. So all those brigades that were employed in this combat mission towards or on Trnovo, they arrived after us. At what time exactly I don't know, but most probably in the course of that or the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 31616 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31616 receives number P6929, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I seek clarification --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- with respect to the last answer. You were asked -- you were talking about the units who arrived later than your unit. Are these units who arrived later the Sarajevo Mechanized Brigade, the 1st Sarajevo Mechanised Brigade and the 2nd Sarajevo Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're asking me if those are the units. If you are asking me specifically to name the units, I can't really answer it clearly because I don't know. But as for the units from the Sarajevo-Romanija or the Herzegovina Corps, these units - after the first small group of people entered Trnovo - these units came after us. They entered the city, the town, without fighting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You said these units. Are these the units I asked you about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't tell you exactly which units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm still a bit --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- confused. Because in the answer you just gave you were talking about units from the SRK and the -- or the Herzegovina Corps. Now, in your statement I only read that units that were with you when you went to Trnovo, although they arrived later, are units of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. Were they or were there units of the Herzegovina Corps involved as well? Or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do know. Let me try to clarify this. We were in the area of responsibility and subordinated to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, and as can you see from this order we received the order from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and we implemented, carried out that order in full. Now after a small group entered, including the commander of the Main Staff, after us the other units from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and the Herzegovina Corps entered. So both of these corps. But they came from different directions. Now if you would like to know the axis of their movement, I can tell you that too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'm not asking you that. When you said this commander of the -- of the Main Staff was included in the small group that entered. Commander of the Main Staff of what exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of the Army of Republika Srpska, General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you say he was with you when the small group entered first Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With me. With me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was there with him. But he is more deserving as far as entering is concerned than I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've answered the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm going to change topics and we're just going to finish with two brief other topics here and then we'll be done. Is it correct that General Mladic ordered the arrest of members of UNPROFOR and international humanitarian organisations in the event of NATO air-raids against RS units and facilities?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: All right. Let's look at something specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 31617.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could already answer the question --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- whenever.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ever. Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we're talking about Lukavac 93, never was an order issued to anyone. If later, I mean, what happened, I was not at that location then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I tried to not confuse the topics and make clear to you that I was changing topics, so the topic I changed to was whether you were aware General Mladic --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Did General Mladic ever order the arrest of members of UNPROFOR in the event of NATO air-raids against RS units or facilities?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ever. That's a bit too broad. Please. There are concrete results. That did occur. But then in that unit the 1st Motorised Guards Brigade, I wasn't serving there. I was serving in Bileca, so I don't know what to say to you with regard to that question. I don't know. I don't have that information and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the question was whether you have any knowledge of General Mladic ordering the arrest of members of UNPROFOR at whatever point in time. Are you aware of General Mladic issuing such an order or do you say, no, I never -- I have no knowledge about him issuing such an order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard about that, but I, for instance, have not received such an order. I did hear that people were tied to light houses, members of UNPROFOR were being brought in, but that is guess-work. And, please, I don't wish to talk about guess-work. I am here to tell you about what I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fully understood. When did you learn about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a long time-period. You're taking me 20 years back now. I found out, say, on TV, through the news, newspapers. Somehow I did find out. People talk. I mean, what can I tell you? Well, you know yourself, don't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, my next question would have been how did you learn about it, but if I listen carefully to your answer, I understand that you learned from it -- learned it through the media and by rumours. Any other source of information apart from those that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You were a member of the 1st Guards Brigade, actually a part of its command staff, in 1994; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 316 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: One second. Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 31617 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 19 April 1994 VRS Main Staff order from General Mladic to the VRS corps and your brigade, among other units, to the commands specifically. We see it is based on a verbal order from the RS president, Radovan Karadzic. Directing your attention to item 4 of the order, where General Mladic orders: "Immediately increase measures for the security and control of UNPROFOR and international humanitarian organisations. In the event of massive air-raids against RS units and facilities, disarm them and arrest them [sic] immediately, confiscate their weapons and combat equipment and use them for PVB," which is indicated as "anti-aircraft warfare." Sir, as a member of the Command Staff that -- that received this order, how are you not aware of it?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's the date on this order? Could you please give me an answer to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: April 1994, Witness. The 19th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Well, as you assume, I have told you through my answers up until now where I was then. When this order arrived - 1994? - is it 1994 or -- no, 1994, yes. Yes. I've lost sight of this. I don't remember this order now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you that General Mladic did issue such orders in 1994, in April of 1994.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I was on leave. Maybe I was somewhere. I don't remember this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution will tender the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31617 receives number P6930, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6930 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this will be my final topic to discuss with you today. In paragraph 9 of your statement, you state as part of a paragraph: "The brigade fought the enemy honourably and not a single crime has ever been attributed to it." This is your evidence; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Wilful abandonment is a serious crime in the military; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A court-martial should have such persons executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P5060 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, do you read paragraph 9, especially in view of the last ten words, approximately, to also deal with crimes committed against the internal order?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I view that as in addition. That it's a general statement, followed then more specific information related to what you just said. Is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I don't think it's fully clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, the Chamber is inclined not to read the last -- well, let's say, the last portion of the sentence as adding something to what previously --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but rather as explaining what was said before; that is, fighting the enemy honourably. Fighting the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I don't want to -- I don't want to have any discussion in front of the witness about it at this moment. But from your first question if you would read it entirely differently, then you would first have to clarify the issue with the witness because then apparently there are several ways of understanding his statement in this respect and we should find out what he meant. So, therefore, I'm not --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sorry, I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- opposing against putting any further questions on it but at least this issue should be resolved before we [Overlapping speakers] follow-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sure. No problem. Well, I -- I agree, I think it's unclear and we should ask the witness. So I agree with Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So I leave it to you how to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, your statement reads: "In executing its combat tasks," then there is a hyphen, "and throughout the war it executed combat tasks," and then another hyphen, "the brigade fought the enemy honourably and not a single crime has ever been attributed to it," and then there's another hyphen, "neither a crime against captured enemy soldiers nor against civilian population." Maybe the most -- fairer thing to do is: What are you trying to say here? Are you saying that these are things that relate to the execution of combat tasks? Are you saying three separate things, or are these three things that you list between the hyphens somehow related?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And I do have a B/C/S version, Your Honours, if he needs to see. Oh. And, Your Honours, actually Ms. Stewart brought to my attention that actually in the B/C/S it does not appear with the hyphens. So I'm not sure if this translation is actually full on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then -- okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should put that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Could we please have paragraph 9 of Exhibit D786.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess part of the confusion on the part of the Chamber, sir, is your reference in relation to this paragraph to wilful abandonment of duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I will eventually come back to this in later questions, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If can you separate it from this paragraph, we'll follow you perhaps better.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But because you put the two together --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: All right. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This is what we want to understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that I can even finish this without even making reference to the paragraphs. If it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I see -- I see you're -- so noted. I'm just going to continue on. Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P5060 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a 7 November 1994 order from General Mladic. It discusses the wilful abandonment of the 1st Guards Brigade forward command post in Ostojici. Under item 1, General Mladic orders the apprehension and initiation of proceedings, criminal proceedings, in the 1st Guards Brigade against you and Colonel Stupar for abandoning this command post. Is it correct that you committed this crime by leaving your post to go to Kalinovik?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, Mr. Weber, I am very glad that you've raised this question and that you've put it forth here for public debate. I have been suffering on account of this for 20 years. You have freed me of this rage and this suffering. And from this moment, I feel rehabilitated. I'm going to tell you the truth here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm just asking you --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, you started your --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Witness, please listen to me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. One second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm listening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber put to a question. Whether that is a relief to you or not, how you emotionally experience that question is not an issue that should be raised. If you're happy --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you're happy that he deals with the matter, that's okay, but please focus on answering his question and the question was whether you had committed the crime of abandoning the command post by going to Kalinovik. Did you do that, or did you not do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please. Please, may I just say something else. Please allow me to say this. It has to do with me. Somebody else should speak about this but I want to say this to you. This order is a forgery. This is abuse of authority, abuse of power. This is a different person. Not the commander of the General Staff, General Mladic. General Mladic did not sign this. This was done behind his back. Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, I'll stop you there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you've asked me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I have not asked you that. I asked you whether you committed that crime and that was what Mr. Weber asked you and you have clearly answered that you did not commit that crime. Now you add that something, which way apparently upsets Mr. Mladic, who is now to sit down immediately -- sit down, Mr. Mladic. Mr. Mladic, sit down and don't speak aloud. Okay. Now, I take it that -- I do not know, as a matter of fact, but certainly if the Defence is surprised by this document - I do not know whether they are or not - they'll certainly ask for more time to explore the matter. But I do understand from Mr. Stojanovic that he is not surprised at all, so if there is any matter to be raised further the Defence will do that when re-examining you. At this moment, please focus on answering the questions that are put to you by Mr. Weber, and you have given a clear answer, you did not commit that crime. You even added, although it wasn't asked, that you considered the document which is shown to you to be a forgery. Next question for Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, in fact, you were detained as a result of this order; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Weber. Mr. Stojanovic, any questions in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A few, Your Honour, and I don't think this is going to take very long. I also appreciate the effort made by our witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask in view of your experience and the rank you held, please tell the Chamber whether an official document of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska would have to have at the end of the text a signature and a stamp of the commander of the organ that is adopting this document?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The second thing I want to ask you: A document, that is a document of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska and that constitutes the conclusions of the Main Staff regarding an assessment of the situation in the theatre of war, would entail the need to familiarise the subordinate units about this as in any organised army?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The questions are getting leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's very leading, Mr. Stojanovic. Now the witness has answered the question, but would you please refrain from leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Could we please have P3071 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, this is the last warning. We do not accept you standing up or speaking aloud. If it happens again, you'll be removed from the courtroom. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, sir, you see the document before you, the one that you had the opportunity to comment upon a moment ago. It says that it is a document of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. There is a number, there is a date, and then in the right-hand corner there is just this hyphen. My question: A document like this, conclusions of the Main Staff assessing the situation, would that have to be sent to the subordinated units of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. And here it cannot be seen whether this document was sent to anyone at all or to whom it was sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now let us look at the last page of this document. My question: During your long career, did you ever have an opportunity of coming across a document that at the end of the text did not have a signature or a stamp or the name of the author of the document?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never came across such a document, and I believe that this is an invalid document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next thing I wish to ask you: During the war, during all of those years of war, did you have any operative knowledge at any point in time that within UNPROFOR there were persons that had the task of guiding the air force to targets of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
