utterances.text: Well, this is a form of special warfare that many armies in the world use against their enemies. That's what SFOR did, UNPROFOR, international forces. They have resources for everything. They have a response for everything. And during combat operations, we knew what the boundaries of our own power were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In case of a NATO bombing of facilities and units of the Army of Republika Srpska, according to the position that was held by your unit too, would that mean that UNPROFOR had sided with one of the warring parties in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I would resist such forces with all means that are available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: He has answered but the question was speculative, the form of question. It also called for a conclusion. It's not eliciting facts at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it was leading. Mr. Stojanovic, these are at least three useful comments which might assist you in phrasing your next question in a more appropriate way. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I will finish with the following question. Colonel, during the preparation for your appearance before the Court, I had occasion to see a lot of documents, the last of which had been presented to you by the Prosecution. Now I would like you to briefly, as briefly as you can, tell this Court why you answered the way you did and why you feel that you had not committed any kind of violation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wait. Stop. One second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please allow me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. One second. You can answer part of that question. We -- the way -- why you answered the question the way you did is not something that is relevant for us. But what you feel is also not of primary importance for us. Apparently you take the view that you did not commit that crime. You can briefly explain to us the factual circumstances on which that opinion is based. So tell us what happened briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Facts, well, first, the order - and I've already said this - this order was not signed by the commander, General Mladic. It's a forgery and an abuse of official authority by another person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I stop you again. I stop you again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where else -- what else can I tell you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you say I never went to Kalinovik, therefore I didn't commit that crime, or I was after being arrested it was established within two days that it had got nothing to do with me, these are all facts. Your opinion about whether the document is a forgery or not, that is what the parties will further discuss. And you don't have to argue on that. But tell us what happened factually which makes you convinced that you did not commit that crime.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, first, let me say this. I was a member of the 1st Guards Motorised Brigade. I had a high degree of authority over the entire complement. Somebody didn't like that. The Guards Brigade had its war path, and it was determined to carry out its tasks professionally. Many people did not like that and one unit had occasion, or actually it happened to the unit, it so happened that that entire personnel left the -- the spot, it was at battalion level, they fled and then in a day or two the enemy arrived and they captured their technical assets. In order to cover this up, the -- this was -- claiming that this was under the command or rather in the area of the Guards Brigade, although this technical equipment was never in the area of the Guards Brigade, somebody used this to actually accuse the responsible officers for this area of responsibility, and that was the two of us, and they accused us of this. But this is not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Simply, you said: A unit at the battalion level. What was the name of the unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a unit that was not within the complement of the 1st Guards Motorised Brigade. It was under the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I wasn't asking who commanded that unit. My question was: What was that unit; that is, what was the name of that unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know exactly its name. It was the armoured mechanised battalion of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You were talking about a person, or persons, or a group that disliked all this. Do you have any knowledge about names or could you otherwise describe that group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not sure I understood you quite clearly. What group are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say somebody used this to accuse the responsible officers for this. And later you said, They accused of this. And you said it's not true. Who accused you? What person or what persons accused you of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was accused by the officers who actually had command over that battalion. They blamed the Guards Brigade and the responsible officers from the Guards Brigade that were at the IKM at that time, the Guards Brigade IKM.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have any names?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not receive interpretation. Could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps the witness should have the opportunity to explain this -- well, I'll repeat it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I asked a question, and I expect the witness to answer that question. Witness, do you have any names of those who accused you?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will reiterate, Your Honour, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I just would appreciate it if the witness feels that should be necessary, if he is about to mention specific names, that perhaps we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, at this moment I do not see any specific reason why we would need to move, and the witness has not applied for that. Do you know any of the names of those who accused you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These were people who were protecting themselves and one man from -- I can't tell you publicly the names. If we can move to closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What's the reason why you can't tell us? Or perhaps you explain that in private session, why you have a reason not to tell us in open session. We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber leaves the topic as it is. Mr. Stojanovic. Any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And we would like to thank the colonel on behalf of General Mladic for his testimony and appearance before this court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions in --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Moloto has one or more questions for you, and Judge Moloto, I'm just addressing you, do you think we can deal with it in a one or two -- a few minutes, because otherwise we would take the break. We're not yet at the break time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I just want to seek one answer and depending on -- one question, and depending on the answer that [Inaudible].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You mentioned that you were detained as a result of these allegations. Who detained you?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably the person who issued that order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was ordered to go --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Witness, I beg your pardon. You must have seen the person who came to say to you, I'm taking you into detention. So I don't expect you to say most probably. You must have seen the person who physically took you into detention. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two policemen and a commander --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Their names, please.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- who were charged with taking the two of us into a detention facility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Their names.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, you say they were charged with --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Who had charged them with that task?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Ratko Vucetic charged them with that task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions. Then, Mr. Sarenac, this concludes your testimony. I would like to thank you very much it -- no, before I do so, I have one question for you, a short one. Earlier Mr. Weber put a question to you where I got the feeling that you might have misunderstood that question. That was a question where you answered, well, we don't have a radio, video, no television, so how could we possibly have instilled fear on the Muslims. You remember that question and that answer you gave? Otherwise I'll read it to you literally, but if you remember that would be --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, I remember it. I remember it. I remember both the question and my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I got the feeling that you may have misunderstood the question. So therefore, I'll try to --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that still has to be established. I would, as a matter of fact, like to put the question or a similar question again to you - I'm looking at Mr. Weber to see whether I -- I understood his question well - and I would invite you to answer that question. What Mr. Weber did put to you was that you, by performing your duties as an assistant commander for morale, religious, and legal affairs, that by performing those duties, you gave support to operations which Mr. Weber, on the basis of documents, believes to have been aimed at the objectives described in those documents, including that Muslims should leave territories or, if they had left already, that they should not return. That is what Mr. Weber put to you, that by doing your job, that you supported what he reads was the aim of all that in the documents. Could you please comment on that?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood Mr. Weber to imply that I, too, was part of this propaganda machine and that I -- that had an influence on the feelings and fear of the other side, and I replied that we didn't have any technical means for any type of propaganda and fear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me stop you there because there's where the misunderstanding may be. I think Mr. Weber also included by performing your duties as an assistant commander for morale, religious, and legal affairs, so irrespective of whether you used radio or television but by giving support to those operations with the aim of those operations as he found them in those documents, that you also participated and that you also supported or were part of that machinery which had those aims in their operations.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, please, you have to understand. It was war time. There were three warring parties. Everything else should be clear from that. We were at war. We didn't cuddle each other. It was a bloody, fierce war, unfortunately, with many casualties, many dead, many people missing. Many traumas remain and all the ethnicities in Bosnia and Herzegovina are suffering from it, and that's very difficult. And I think that from this, it must be clear to you what my aspirations are, where I stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At least now I have the feeling that you commented on the question as it was intended and clarified to you. Have this triggered any further questions? Not. Then I started already thanking you. I continue that. I would like to thank you very much for having come to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties, by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, allow me to say thank you and to say that I appreciate you having me here as a witness, and I also wish you success in your work. And I would like to greet all of your associates as well as General Mladic. He was my war time commander, so please bear with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think you were instructed by the Victims and Witness Section not to do what you did last, isn't it? You, nevertheless, did it. Okay. It's not appreciated. Please follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't instructed by the Victims and Witness Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll verify that. If it has not been done, then, of course, you can forget about it. But if you were instructed not to send any personal greetings to the accused, then we'll verify that. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just because it's not clear what just happened on the actual written record, I believe the witness saluted General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, he did that briefly. You may follow the usher. And, again, a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, any challenge of the authenticity of any document which has been admitted previously should take the form of a reconsideration of the decision on admission rather than to let a witness tell us that a document is a forgery. If he has any facts to his knowledge, ask about those facts. But that's the proper way of dealing with the matter. And I think that both of the documents that you asked questions about, whether he had ever seen a document unsigned, well, this Chamber has seen documents unsigned, so the witness must have not looked very well, perhaps, at the time or may have missed something. But we're always open for questions of authenticity. First of all they should be raised, first, at the time a document is tendered. I think for the last one authenticity was not raised. There was an objection against that document but not, as far as I understand, on the basis of authenticity but you'd rather prefer to have it introduced through a live witness. But whatever it is, a new decision requires a motion to reconsider and that should have a proper factual basis. Leave it to that. We take a break and we'll resume at 20 minutes to 1.00. And is the Defence ready to call its next witness? We -- we take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the witness to enter the courtroom, the Chamber wondered, since we had a bit of a delayed start, whether we could not have a little bit over one hour and then finish for the day. And then the parties are urged to see whether it would be possible to conclude the testimony of this witness - it's only a very short statement - today.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it will be all right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I see that Mr. MacDonald is also nodding in the affirmative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Djeric. My I invite you to make the solemn declaration, of which the text is now handed out to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr. Djeric. You will first be examined by Mr. Stojanovic. You'll find him to your left. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, good afternoon and welcome to this courtroom. Could you please state for the record slowly your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: My name is Zoran Djeric.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djeric, at one point in time, did you make a statement to the Defence of General Mladic, a written statement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we please have in e-court 65 ter 1D01692.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djeric, you can see before you on the screen a statement, and I would like you to tell the Court whether the signature on this page of this written statement is yours.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see the last page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djeric, does your signature appear on the last page of this statement? What you see here, is that your signature and did you date this statement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is my signature, and I also entered the date in my own hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like to look at paragraph 7 of this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the first sentence, we see a date. It says: "It was only in November 1992 ..." Now, Mr. Djeric, let me ask you this: Did you point out to me before you came to this courtroom that it should read -- that this should actually read "it was only in December 1992"?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. It should be it was only in December 1992. There should be a correction there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now that you've corrected this date, if I were to put the same questions to you today in this courtroom, now that you've taken this solemn oath, would your answers be identical to those contained in this corrected written statement that is before you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes, they would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender the statement of Zoran Djeric, 1D01692 being the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1692 receives number D788, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D788 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave at this point in time I would like to read out the summary of Witness Zoran Djeric's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The statement is one page and a half, so the summary is supposed to be pretty much shorter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly, Your Honour. Up until the war, the witness, Zoran Djeric, worked in Rogatica in the wood processing industry. It is that position that he held when the war broke out in 1992 in his town. The witness will testify about a deterioration in inter-ethnic relations from the autumn of 1991 about the arming of Muslims, about the organisation of patrols among the local population, and about people leaving his area to join the National Guards Corps, ZNG, and to go to Vukovar. In April 1992 with his family he left the town of Rogatica as a precaution, because he lived in a part of town where the majority population was Muslim. Immediately upon arriving in his native village, he joined the self-organised Serb village guards. Up until 1992, they did not have any contact with the VRS and they acted with full independence on the basis of the principle of self-organisation. It is only at the end of June or beginning of July 1992 that these self-organised units were all linked up in an integrated system. In December 1992 after the attack on Sjemec, he was assigned to the mortar squad of the Rogatica Brigade and remained in that position until the end of the war. He is aware that in December 1992 a group of Muslims took a bus from Rogatica to Olovo, but the Muslims would not take them in. So when they returned to Rogatica, the municipal authorities put them up in a facility that was called Rasadnik. Otherwise, he himself had his Muslim friends stay at his place. But when the war broke out, as he was unable to guarantee their safety, they left his house. Finally, he says that he is unaware of any kind of unlawful order aimed against the Muslims or any organised activities against Muslim civilians. Your Honours, that is the summary of this witness's statement. Allow me, just briefly, to put a question to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please have D788 in e-court. And could we focus on paragraph 4 of this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You see it before you now, Mr. Djeric. It is paragraph 4 of your statement. And you say that you left town and that was done for the sake of prevention, as a precaution, because it was impossible to have an evacuation. Could you please explain to the Court what the real reasons were when you described it this way, the real reasons for your decision in April 1992 to leave Rogatica with your family.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: In the street where I lived before the war conflict broke out in Rogatica, there were about ten Serb houses. The rest were Muslim houses. So as the minority population in the territory of the municipality and in that street, we had to evacuate for the sake of prevention because, quite simply, conflict was hanging in the air. Since we did not have the possibility to evacuate later as things developed, we decided to do it on time, if I can put it that way. That proved out to be good, correct, and true, for my family and for the other families from that street. That is what I can say about that. And if there's anything else, I am prepared to answer any other questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the area where you lived, were there any other families of Serb ethnicity that decided to leave Rogatica for the same reason before the armed conflict broke out?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I've mentioned that in my statement. As far as I can remember, people also decided to leave because our position was such that there was no possibility for us to evacuation in one direction only, eastward, that is to say, towards the Karanfeld [phoen] Street where the majority population was Serb. We were in an industrial zone and we could not go north or south or west, especially during the night if there were to be some incidents then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to end with the following question: Did you notice whether there were any neighbours of yours who were of Muslim ethnicity who, before the armed conflict broke out, left Rogatica as well?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: As far as I knew, as I socialised with these people, it was mainly women and children that were leaving. Also for the sake of prevention because no one could forecast when the clashes would start and what their that nature would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djeric, thank you. At this point in time we have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Before I give an opportunity to the Prosecution to cross-examine you, I've one question in relation to your statement. Did you study the indictment against Mr. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I am aware of some details, but I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do you know about charges in relation to events in Rasadnik? Do you know what he's charged with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for these events in Rasadnik, I've referred to that in my statement. One group of people who were put up there later, in December, were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, I'm going to stop you. Could you tell us what you know about the charges? What do the charges say about an event in Rasadnik, the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I haven't seen that. I really haven't seen that. If you explain it to me, I'll try to answer. I don't know exactly what the charges are in relation to Rasadnik. Is it ethnic cleansing or is it something else?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, your statement reads: "As regards the Rasadnik incident referred to in the indictment," and then you give some comments. Therefore, I wondered whether you are aware of what is in the indictment in relation to Rasadnik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just know that a certain number of people of Muslim ethnicity were staying there. I know that. I can say that. I knew some of these people who were there. That is what I stated in my statement. I don't know if I understood the question correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the question simply was if you are commenting on what is in the indictment about an event in Rasadnik, I was wondering whether you had knowledge what is in the indictment about Rasadnik. But apparently I do understand that you have no knowledge about what Mr. Mladic is charged with in relation to Rasadnik. Which is okay. I mean, but ... Do you know or don't you know? If you don't know, just tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. MacDonald. You'll now be cross-examined by Mr. MacDonald. Mr. MacDonald is counsel for the Prosecution, and you find him to your right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: In your statement at paragraphs 3 and 4, you state that you moved to Borike and joined the Serb guards in April 1992. Your commander there was Rajko Kusic. That's right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So you were, in effect, part of the Rogatica Serbian Territorial Defence. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Your unit was deployed in sections and platoons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If I can take you to the first line of paragraph 6 of your statement. We actually have it on the screen in front of us already. It states: "By at least mid-1992, we had no contacts with the army and we literally operated on the principle of self-organisation." But it is actually true that by the end of April 1992, your commander, Rajko Kusic, was reporting about your unit's location, tasks, and weaponry to the JNA, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Over there where I was, that is where local guards were organised, and we spent most of our time there until we were asked to go to different points. That was the beginning of the war; that is to say, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Who asked to you go to different points?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: When I went to the separation line in 1992, then I was called by the command. This was in December after our positions at Mount Sjemec were attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Sorry, in your previous answer, you said: "We spent most of our time there until we were asked to go to different points. That was the beginning of the war ..." So I understood that you were asked to move in April of 1992. Is that right or wrong?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: No, no. We were local guards. There's -- that was guard duty that we had and we were providing security for our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution please have P06814 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: This is a report on 30th of April, 1992, on the combat readiness of the Territorial Defence units. It's from the command of the Territorial Defence battalion in Rogatica, and it's signed by Rajko Kusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can have page 4 in the English and page 2 in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djeric, if I can ask you to lack at the bottom of the B/C/S document on the screen in front of you, three units up, as it were, do you see the words "territorially based detachment, Borike."

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And the first part states: "Deployed per platoons and sections." And you confirmed that you were deployed in platoons and sections and it lists a number of different areas. Were you deployed in those areas?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: For a while, perhaps in the beginning of May, I was securing the IKM at Borike. That is all, in addition to the local guards until the beginning of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: You were securing an IKM. That's a forward command post, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes, in one period of time. And then we were returned to provide local guard duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Who ordered you to secure the IKM at Borike in the beginning of May?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Well, we received orders from the IKM. I'm certainly not going to say that it was the beginning of May, but it was during the month of May and not earlier than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: You received orders from the IKM. Who was based at the IKM? Who was giving you those orders?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: We received that orally by radio communication from the command of the IKM that we should report at Borike to provide security for the IKM.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, I appreciate it's from the command of the IKM. Who was that? Which unit?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Well, units of the Territorial Defence of that place; that is to say, Borike itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Perhaps if we turn back to the document in front of you, you'll see in the next two paragraphs, after it says deployed per platoons and sections, there are the words: "Control and closing down of the axis," and it says that's towards a number of areas, and then it gives a list of the weaponry in the unit. Firstly, do you recognise that that is the weaponry that you had in your unit?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Well, the weaponry was mostly long barrels, semi-automatic rifles, M48 rifles, and automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Perhaps if we can go back to the first page in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Witness, near the top of this document before the main body, do you see the words "pursuant to order dated 21st April 1992, I hereby submit a report ... " Do you see those words?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution please now have P06813 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Witness, this is an order from the command of the 1st Romanija Brigade to the battalion of the Territorial Defence, Rogatica, for delivery of reports regarding Territorial Defence unit battle readiness. Do you see it is dated 21st April 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So your commander, Rajko Kusic, is responding to an order to report on the battle readiness of, amongst others, your unit. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So, Witness, your commander reporting to an order of this brigade command. Clearly you did have contact with the army. This contradicts what you said in your statement, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: I said that we were not linked up. As far as the command is concerned, our commander, I'm not saying that they were not linked up as far as these events are concerned, and I'm not saying that they did not have any contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to read the first sentence of paragraph 6 of your statement back to you. At just the first part: "By at least mid-1992, we had no contacts with the army." Now, that's not correct, is it.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: That is our knowledge. Perhaps I do not remember some dates literally so that I could put them in a particular sequence as required by the statement. Perhaps I did not link up all of this properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. I'd now like to play a video --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, Mr. -- You say, I didn't have the chronology on my mind. In your statement, you say calls were sent to us to report to the meeting point in Borike where we would be given further assignments, but this did not happen until July 1992. You told us a few minutes ago that you'd go to the IKM late -- in late May or early June, and certainly before July, that contradicts your statement where it gives a very precise time indication. Do you have any explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a short period of time, perhaps five, six, or seven days that we provided security there. And then we returned again, I mean, to provide security in our native villages. Again, perhaps in these statements I did not give the exact sequence of these events, but it was a short period. So it wasn't non-stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, to reveal that there was an IKM and that you were ordered to go there would also reveal that it was not just self-organised. Would you agree with me? Even if only for a short period of time that at least you were part of a greater context, a greater organised force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Later we became linked up in a more organised set-up and that is what I said in my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I put to you is that by not saying anything about the five or six days, that this might well introduce a wrong impression of the real situation. If you have any comment to it, please give it. Otherwise, I'll ask Mr. MacDonald to continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't have any comment to that. Perhaps I omitted something in my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'd now seek to play a video, Your Honours. It is approximately four minutes long and there are three different clips. The transcripts, I think, have been handed out to the booths, although I'm afraid I didn't get it checked with CLSS beforehand, so we will have to play it twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, we'll look at the video twice, that's for very technical reasons, and give you an opportunity to carefully see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour. I didn't give the 65 ter number. It is 22430b.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Djeric --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have to look at it twice, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Ah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the Chamber to understand what the video tells us --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I was just going to ask him to identify the person in the clip just now, but I'm happy for it to be run through it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. And then we return through it again. You can put that question. Do you recognise the person speaking on the video-clip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rajko Kusic, the commander of the light brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now next time if you do that, don't give his name on the video itself so that might bring some thoughts. But let's look at it again so that we also know what Mr. Kusic tells us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I would seek after each clip to ask a question, Your Honours. Is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can do it portion by portion. Unless there is a relation or whether the following portion sheds some light on it, and then of course it would be a -- a waste of time to limit ourselves to -- but if it's limited to that portion, fine. Please proceed. So we first now look at the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] Of the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade is particular in many mays. First what is particular is its beginning. The embryo of the brigade was created on 6 March 1992 as a forward section of the 216th Brigade of the former Yugoslav People's Army with the headquarters in Han Pijesak. After the mobilisation and the secession of Slovenia and Croatia had taken place, the decisions on withdrawing the JNA and the mobilising in Bosnia and Herzegovina brought about the mobilisation of the 216th Brigade. "Some military conscripts from the municipality of Rogatica, who had not been assigned to the 216th Brigade, were within the strength of the Territorial Defence of the former Army of Yugoslavia in the territory of the Rogatica municipality. Together with some other military conscripts from the municipality, I was one of those. "Since the TO failed to function and the SDA mostly carried out the setting up of their armed forces of the Ministry of Interior, the Green Berets, and the TO did not function; that is, it was not functioning. By creating armed forces of the Muslim army through the MUP and the party of SDA, some of the military conscripts volunteers as reinforcement of the 216th Brigade, and since they were stationed in Gucevo and Han Pijesak and a battalion of military conscripts from this area was in Gucevo, we had gathered on a voluntary basis, about 50 volunteers, and expressed a desire to join the defence of the state, and a reinforced platoon was formed which remained in this area, the Borike location, which came out in Borike on 6 March 1992 under the command of the 216th Brigade. That was the first embryo of the brigade."

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honours, the video has been stopped at 02:13:03.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Djeric, this -- this is your commander stating that the unit in Borike came out on 6 March 1992 and was under the command of the 216th Brigade. You must have known that the unit you were joining was under the command of that brigade when you joined it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I was a member of the reserve corps of the 216th Brigade in Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: When were you a member of the reserve corps?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Before the war broke out, in the 1990s, in 1990 and 1991, Autumn of 1991, when the Muslims deserted the unit. We reinforced that unit as a reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So if I've understood you correctly, in autumn 1991 you reinforced the 216th Brigade as part of their reserve corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes. But even earlier on, that was my war time deployment and some -- every two or three years we would have exercises where we would be deployed at Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I would seek to play the next portion of the video Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we ask, the 6th of March which is mentioned as the date of, if I could say, the rebirth or the -- does that ring a bell to you that there was activity on the 6th of March as described by Mr. Kusic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time I was in Rogatica and I'm not very familiar with those activities, the coming out of men in that territory. I was still engaged and I had some activities within my company, so I'm not really familiar with the very beginnings, the events at the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do you mean by your company? That's an ambiguous term. In English at least.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I mean, the work organisation where I worked, the enterprise, the company, the lumber industry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you were not in way aware involved in the restart of the -- of the unit Mr. Kusic is talking about? You say I'm not very familiar, which is a bit of an ambiguous term as well. Did you know about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, partly. I knew something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What did you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I knew that a unit was being established which was, as the commander said, the embryo of the Serbian army in those areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when you earlier testified that you were sent to secure the IKM in -- certainly before July, was that in the same context of that unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did see some officers from time to time, but these men who were there, I didn't see them in that environment, when I went to secure the IKM.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The men who were with Commander Kusic at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But Commander Kusic is talking about Borike, isn't it? Were there more units or more command posts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I too am referring to Borike.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But there was only one unit, one command post in Borike?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, that is so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. MacDonald. We play now the second part? Yes. We re-play now the second part of the interview. Please carefully listen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] The company that was then within the strength of the 216th Brigade and together with that battalion took part for the first time in Visegrad from the 18th to 22nd of April 1992, where they eliminated the Green Berets; that is, where the Muslims rebelled in order to create the border with Serbia that is to secede from Yugoslav which was the main objective. "The units took part in co-operation with a battalion of the 216th Brigade of the Uzice Corps in order to calm the situation down; that is, they did not act offensively but in order to protect the Serb civilians. That took place between 18th and 22nd of April. They continued to exist within the 216th Brigade which provided security to the civilians and maintained order in the region of Podrinje from Visegrad, Medjedja, Ustipraca, Gorazde."

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Near to the time -- ah. For the record, the video is stopped at 03:22:08. Near to the time you joined this unit in Borike, a company took part in combat operations in Visegrad with the 216th Brigade, and then continued to exist within the 216th Brigade in that region. You must have known about that as well.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that based on this statement. But also when I was there, I was briefed. Although, I did not take part in those offensive operations but I am aware of that event. And we could see it here, too, in this video insert.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I seek to play the last portion of the video, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look at the last portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] With the decision of the 19th of May on the establishment of the VRS, it was obvious to us, and we took that road, to organise ourselves on instructions and creating units with all elements of the system of command and control."

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Djeric, now, your unit joined the VRS on 19 May 1992, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes. Up until then the former Yugoslav People's Army was the only legitimate regular military force in Bosnia-Herzegovina. On the 19th of May, the Army of Republika Srpska was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could the witness also answer your question, preferably. And your unit joined the VRS on the 19th of May, once it was established?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And the Prosecution seeks to tender the video-clip, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, I take it that you're waiting to receive the CD.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's there, almost. Madam Registrar once you've receive the CD, could you assign a number to the video.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Document 22430b receives number P6931, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6931 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'd seek to move on to my final topic, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Djeric, at the end of your statement, you say: "None of the orders I am aware of was illegal." For the sake of clarity, do you accept there may have been illegal orders and you were simply not aware of them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: I was not aware of any such orders, but I cannot claim that there were none. As far as I knew, all orders were within the bounds of the Geneva Conventions on war activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Nothing further, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. MacDonald. Mr. Stojanovic, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The video that now bears the number P6931, if I jotted that down correctly, with the assistance of Ms. Stewart, I would appreciate if we could see the part from 01:40 through 02:00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the portion. It is not properly recorded?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will repeat that, Your Honours. So I would seek the assistance of Ms. Janet, could we begin with 01:40 up until 02:00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we start this portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] We gathered on a voluntary basis about 40 volunteers and expressed a desire to join the defence of the state and a reinforced platoon was established which remained in this area, the Borike location."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djeric, now in this excerpt, and you had occasion to hear it for the third time, Kusic said: "We had gathered on a voluntary basis about 40 volunteers and expressed a desire to join the defence of the state..." Now, my question is this: Did you at any point in time during that period, or up until today, have any information about the manner in which these people began gathering, beginning with the 6th of March, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Well, as Mr. Kusic said in his statement, everything was organised on a voluntary basis. I can say that there was a very difficult heritage in those areas, historical heritage, and people organised themselves lest, heaven forbid, 1941 should repeat itself. That is what I know about the organisation from these beginnings.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will conclude with the following question in view of your last answers given to my learned friend, Mr. Prosecutor. When did you, in your village, learn and when did you organise yourselves as members of the VRS? When did you learn of it and when did you organise?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Well, after it was established on the 19th of May, that is when we joined the Army of Republika Srpska because up until then the Yugoslav People's Army had been the only legitimate armed force. At that time we realised that this force was non-existent and we believed that we had to do something and organise ourselves, if you understand my meaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you, specifically you yourself, when did you for the first time receive your assignment in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: As for the first combat operations, I received a written report on the 20th of December. This is when I was assigned directly to combat operations because in the previous days there was combat activity in the general area --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the place names, two place names, at the end of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djeric, thank you for coming to testify before this Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Djeric, when you said in the previous days there was combat activity in the general area of ... what exactly? Because the interpreters missed what general area you were referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The general area of the Sjemec mountain and the Pesurici village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Before -- I don't know whether you have any questions at this moment. I would have one or two questions for you Witness, Mr. Djeric. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, I am taking you back to paragraph 8 where you are commenting on the Rasadnik incident referred to in the indictment which, by the way, took place as charged in August, but you are commenting on what happened in December, so -- but irrespective of that, you described that Muslims were sent by bus and then refused to enter and then went back to Rogatica, and you said then: "Since they were returned to Rogatica, the municipal authorities placed them at a facility in Rasadnik." And you are saying that this happened in 1992. Why were they placed by the authorities in Rasadnik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Well, this is all I can say about that incident. They were sent on a bus to Olovo where the separation line was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what we find in your statement. What I'd like to know is when they were refused and returned to Rogatica, why were they placed at a facility in Rasadnik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Well, for security reasons they could not return to the area where they had lived before, before -- because the combat operations were under way, and in order to prevent, forestall anything from happening to them, they were put up there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was in December?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Were they given any free choice --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or were they -- so they were not placed but they were given a choice whether to go home or not to go home, and if they did not want to go home, they were placed in Rasadnik? Is that how it happened? If you know. I don't know whether you were present.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: I don't know if they were offered. I wasn't there. But I don't know if they were offered any other option other than they -- than to go for an exchange, towards Olovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Now a minute ago, I asked you, were they given any free choice? You said yes. And on my next question, you now say that you don't know. Are you aware that that is rather confusing for this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreter was late in answering to the previous question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I knew that they were offered the option to go for an exchange, to go to Olovo. Now whether that was their free choice or whether there were any other connotations, I can't really claim with any certainty because I did not take part in those events. I was already --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think this -- this "yes" was misplaced in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- on the front line at that -- in those days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. -- we're still waiting for the translation, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry. I think that this "yes" in line 19 of page 81 was misplaced in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreters informed us about a problem there. But it is clear now that the witness cannot tell us whether a real free choice was given to those who were placed in Rasadnik. I have no further questions. Have my questions trigged any need for further questions? If not, Mr. Djeric, this concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered the questions that were put to you, put to you by the parties and put to you by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for making it possible for me to speak before an organ of justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although there was a decision which I could read but I don't want to stress -- to extend the time too much, unless you say that seven minutes would be okay. But otherwise, I more or less indicated that we would finish after a little bit over one hour. Perhaps it's better to do that. Unless the Defence would strongly encourage me to read the -- you are not, Mr. Lukic. That's clear and fully understandable. I leave it to that. We adjourn for the day and we resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 20th of November, 9.30 in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 20th day of November, 2014, at 9.30 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
